prompt: Use case: identity-preserve. Production transparent animation sprite atlas for Little King. The input image is the reference for ONE existing character or building identity. Preserve its exact outfit, face, colours, species, weapons and silhouette. Warm hand-painted storybook gouache, clear chestnut outlines, pine green, parchment and antique gold, consistent with the input image. Output a SQUARE 2048x2048 RGBA sprite atlas containing EXACTLY FOUR COLUMNS and FOUR ROWS, sixteen equal cells. Exactly ONE complete subject in each cell. Cell centres at 12.5%,37.5%,62.5%,87.5% on each axis. Identical scale, camera and anchor across ALL cells. Upright figures use the SAME foot baseline and head size. Every weapon and appendage stays strictly INSIDE its own cell, with at least 10% transparent padding. Front three-quarter view toward screen right. Absolutely NO background, floor, shadows, grid lines, borders, numbers, letters or labels. True transparent alpha outside each figure. Frames read left to right and top to bottom. A compact medieval siege catapult building, chestnut wooden chassis on four stout wheels, ONE tall throwing arm with stone cup, stone counterweight, wound rope mechanism, moss-green cloth side panel and antique-gold iron bindings. Complete readable three-quarter front view, no crew. Row 1: four subtle idle flag/canopy-sway frames. Row 2: four subtle moving mechanical/flag frames, the building base NEVER walks or changes position. Row 3: four action frames, mechanism ready, draw back, release arrow or stone, recoil and recover; barracks instead opens door and flags lift, no soldier appears. Row 4: first two hit reaction frames (jolt and recover); last two destruction frames (slight structural slump then small collapsed rubble), no explosions. Independently draw genuine successive poses, not sixteen identical copies. No particles or large magic effects. Never crop limbs, weapon tips or the character. No pose crosses cell boundaries. Critical: no flying arrows, detached projectiles, dust or ground shadows. Each subject must fit inside a square cell with a wide 15% transparent margin on every side. Keep the SAME compact scale in all sixteen frames. Make all weapons and wings compact enough to fit fully.
